title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
units.literal: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
units.idiomatic: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

units.zh: 惠帝乃止。
units.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

units.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
units.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
units.idiomatic: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

units.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
units.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

units.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
units.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
units.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

units.zh: 由是奇之。
units.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
units.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

units.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
units.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
units.idiomatic: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

units.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
units.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
units.idiomatic: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

units.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
units.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
units.idiomatic: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

units.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
units.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
units.idiomatic: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

units.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
units.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
units.idiomatic: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

units.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
units.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.
units.idiomatic: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.

units.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
units.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.
units.idiomatic: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.

units.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
units.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
units.idiomatic: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

units.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
units.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.
units.idiomatic: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.

units.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
units.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

units.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
units.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
units.idiomatic: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

units.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
units.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.
units.idiomatic: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.

units.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
units.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.
units.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.

units.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
units.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.
units.idiomatic: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.

title.zh: 卷二十 志第十 禮中
title.raw: 卷二十 志第十 禮中 Volume 20 Treatises 10: Rites Part Two

units.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。
units.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the realm observed mourning for three days only.
units.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao died, the whole state wore mourning for three days and no more.

units.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。
units.literal: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent: once the burial ended he set aside formal mourning, yet still wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich food from his table.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Sima Yan kept the Han–Wei rule of ending court mourning at burial, but he still dressed in plain hemp deep robes, set aside brocade cushions, and ate only coarse fare.

units.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞夏商周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。
units.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.
units.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.

title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

units.zh: 惠帝在東宮，將納妃。
units.literal: When Emperor Hui in Eastern Palace—about to take consort.
units.idiomatic: While Hui was heir they chose a princess.

units.zh: 武帝慮太子尚幼，未知帷房之事，乃遣往東宮侍寢，由是得幸有身。
units.literal: Emperor Wu worried crown prince still young—did not know inner chamber affairs—therefor dispatched go Eastern Palace attend bedding—thereby gained favor pregnant.
units.idiomatic: Wu, worried the crown prince was still young and did not know the affairs of the bedchamber, sent her to the Eastern Palace to attend him in bed—she conceived.

units.zh: 賈后妒忌之，玖求還西宮，遂生愍懷太子，年三四歲，惠帝不知也。
units.literal: Empress Jia jealous—Jiu begged return western palace—thereby bore Crown Prince Minhuai—age three four years—Emperor Hui did not know.
units.idiomatic: Jia drove her west—she bore Minhuai—Hui knew nothing for years.

units.zh: 入朝，見愍懷與諸皇子共戲，執其手，武帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
units.literal: Entering court seeing Minhuai playing with imperial sons—grasped his hand—Emperor Wu said: “This is your son.”
units.idiomatic: Entering court and seeing Minhuai playing with the imperial sons, he took his hand and Emperor Wu said, "This is your son."

units.zh: 及立為太子，拜玖為淑媛。
units.literal: When established crown prince—invested Jiu as Shuyuan.
units.idiomatic: When Minhuai became heir she became Shuyuan.

units.zh: 懷王皇太后諱媛姬，不知所出。
units.literal: Empress Dowager Wang of Huai taboo Yuanji—birth unknown.
units.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang Yuanji—parentage unknown.

units.zh: 初入武帝宮，拜中才人，早卒。
units.literal: First entered Emperor Wu palace—invested Mid-ranked Talented Lady—died early.
units.idiomatic: She entered Wu’s harem as mid-ranked talented lady—died young.

units.zh: 懷帝即位，追尊曰皇太后。
units.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended—posthumously honored Empress Dowager.
units.idiomatic: Huai raised her posthumously to dowager.

title.zh: 卷九十三 列傳第六十三 外戚
title.raw: 卷九十三 列傳第六十三 外戚 Volume 93 Biographies 63: Imperial Affines

units.zh: 逮于晉難，始自宮掖。
units.literal: When it came to the Jin calamity, it began in the palace apartments.
units.idiomatic: The Jin dynasty’s catastrophe began in the inner palace.

units.zh: 楊駿藉武帝之寵私，叨竊非據，賈謐乘惠皇之蒙昧，成此厲階，遂使悼后遇雲林之災，湣懷濫湖城之酷。
units.literal: Yang Jun relied on Emperor Wu’s private favor and grasped what he should not have held; Jia Mi rode Emperor Hui’s dullness and made this stair of evil, so that Empress Dao met disaster at Yunlin, and Min Huai suffered cruel abuse at Hucheng.
units.idiomatic: Yang Jun parlayed Emperor Wu’s favor into a post he never deserved; Jia Mi exploited Emperor Hui’s weakness and laid the steps to ruin—so Empress Dao met disaster at Yunlin, and Min Huai suffered cruel abuse at Hucheng.

units.zh: 天人道盡，喪亂弘多，宗廟以之顛覆，黎庶於焉殄瘁。
units.literal: The way of Heaven and men was exhausted; bereavement and chaos were vast; the ancestral temple thereby was overturned; the common people thereby were worn to the bone.
units.idiomatic: Heaven and earth seemed to abandon the house of Jin; chaos spread without end, the altars fell, and the people were ground down.

units.zh: 及會謀反，琇正言苦諫，還，賜爵關內侯。
units.literal: When Hui plotted rebellion, Xiu with upright words bitterly remonstrated; on returning, he was enfeoffed as Marquis Within the Passes.
units.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui rebelled, Yang Xiu spoke bluntly against it; afterward he was rewarded with the rank of Marquis Within the Passes.

units.zh: 琇涉學有智算，少與武帝通門，甚相親狎，每接筵同席，嘗謂帝曰：「若富貴見用，任領護各十年。」
units.literal: Xiu was versed in learning and had clever reckoning; in youth he shared gate ties with Emperor Wu and was very intimate; whenever they met at feasts on the same mat, he once said to the emperor: ‘If when noble and honored I am employed, let me hold each of Colonel of the Garrison and Protector of the Army for ten years.’
units.idiomatic: Yang Xiu was learned and shrewd; he had known Emperor Wu since youth and they were close. At shared meals he once said, ‘If I rise with you, give me ten years as chief of each guard command.’

units.zh: 帝戲而許之。
units.literal: ’ The emperor in jest assented.
units.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and agreed.

units.zh: 初，帝未立為太子，而聲論不及弟攸，文帝素意重攸，恆有代宗之議。
units.literal: At first, when the emperor had not yet been established as heir apparent, his reputation did not match his younger brother You’s; Emperor Wen had long favored You and constantly had talk of replacing the heir.
units.idiomatic: Before Sima Yan was named heir, opinion favored his younger brother Sima You; Emperor Wen had always preferred You, and courtiers often spoke of making You the successor.

units.zh: 琇密為武帝畫策，甚有匡救。
units.literal: Xiu secretly for Emperor Wu drew plans and had great corrective rescue.
units.idiomatic: Yang Xiu worked behind the scenes for Sima Yan and did much to steady his position.

units.zh: 又觀察文帝為政損益，揆度應所顧問之事，皆令武帝默而識之。
units.literal: Further he observed Emperor Wen’s governance, what was harmful and beneficial, and estimated matters that should be consulted on, all ordering Emperor Wu silently to memorize them.
units.idiomatic: He also studied how Emperor Wen ran the government and guessed what questions might come up, then had Sima Yan commit the answers to memory.

units.zh: 其後文帝與武帝論當世之務及人間可否，武帝答無不允，由是儲位遂定。
units.literal: Thereafter when Emperor Wen discussed with Emperor Wu the tasks of the age and whether affairs among men were feasible or not, Emperor Wu’s answers were without exception fitting; by this the heir’s place was then fixed.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen later quizzed Sima Yan on policy and practical judgment, every reply was apt, and the succession was settled.

units.zh: 及帝為撫軍，命琇參軍事。
units.literal: When the emperor became Army-soothing General, he ordered Xiu to join military affairs.
units.idiomatic: When Sima Yan became General Who Pacifies the Army, he put Yang Xiu on his military staff.

units.zh: 帝即王位後，擢琇為左衛將軍，封甘露亭侯。
units.literal: After the emperor assumed the kingship, he promoted Xiu to General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Sweet-Dew Hamlet.
units.idiomatic: After the emperor assumed the kingship, he raised Yang Xiu to General of the Left Guard and made him Marquis of Sweet-Dew Hamlet.

units.zh: 帝踐阼，累遷中護軍，加散騎常侍。
units.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Central Protector of the Army and added as Regular Cavalier Attendant.
units.idiomatic: After Sima Yan became emperor, Yang Xiu rose step by step to Central Protector of the Army with the additional title of Regular Cavalier Attendant.

units.zh: 琇在職十三年，典禁兵，豫機密，寵遇甚厚。
units.literal: Xiu in office thirteen years commanded the forbidden troops, participated in secret matters, and favor and treatment were very thick.
units.idiomatic: For thirteen years he commanded the palace guard, shared state secrets, and enjoyed extraordinary favor.

units.zh: 然放恣犯法，每為有司所貸。
units.literal: Yet unrestrained he violated the law and was always forgiven by the authorities.
units.idiomatic: He broke the law with impunity; officials usually looked the other way.

units.zh: 其後司隸校尉劉毅劾之，應至重刑，武帝以舊恩，直免官而已。
units.literal: Thereafter Metropolitan Commandant Liu Yi impeached him; it should have reached heavy punishment, but Emperor Wu on account of old favor only dismissed him from office.
units.idiomatic: When Metropolitan Commandant Liu Yi impeached him, the case called for severe penalties, but Emperor Wu settled for stripping him of his post out of old friendship.

units.zh: 尋以侯白衣領護軍。
units.literal: Soon, as marquis in white garments he headed the Protector of the Army.
units.idiomatic: Before long he was allowed to retain his marquisate while serving as Protector of the Army in civilian dress.

units.zh: 拜特進，加散騎常侍，還第，卒。
units.literal: He was appointed Exalted Marcher, added as Regular Cavalier Attendant, returned to his mansion, and died.
units.idiomatic: He was given the honorific Exalted Marcher and Regular Cavalier Attendant, went home, and died.

units.zh: 帝手詔曰：「琇與朕有先後之親，少小之恩，歷位外內，忠允茂著。
units.literal: The emperor’s handwritten edict said: ‘Xiu with Us has closeness of empress and consort, favor from youth, has passed through posts outer and inner, loyalty and trustworthiness luxuriantly manifest.’
units.idiomatic: The emperor wrote by his own hand: ‘Yang Xiu is kin by marriage and has known Us since boyhood; he has served inside and outside the court with conspicuous loyalty.’

units.zh: 不幸早薨，朕甚悼之。
units.literal: ’ Unluckily he died early; We greatly mourn him.
units.idiomatic: His early death grieves Us deeply.’

units.literal: Mencius [text damaged], Kuang and Zhang instructed and explained.

title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

units.zh: 后少聰慧，善書，姿質美麗，閑於女工。
units.literal: The empress was clever from youth, skilled at calligraphy, beautiful in bearing, and adept at women’s crafts.
units.idiomatic: From childhood she was bright and graceful, wrote well, was strikingly beautiful, and excelled at needlework.

units.zh: 有善相者嘗相后，當極貴，文帝聞而為世子聘焉。
units.literal: A skilled physiognomist once read the empress’s features and said she would reach supreme honor; Emperor Wen heard of it and betrothed her to the heir apparent.
units.idiomatic: A physiognomist predicted she would rise to the highest rank, and when Emperor Wen heard this he betrothed her to the crown prince.

units.zh: 甚被寵遇，生毗陵悼王軌、惠帝、秦獻王柬，平陽、新豐、陽平公主。
units.literal: She received great favor and bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.
units.idiomatic: Deeply favored, she bore Prince Gui of Biling, Emperor Hui, Prince Jian of Qin, and the princesses of Pingyang, Xinfeng, and Yangping.

units.zh: 武帝即位，立為皇后。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he established her as empress.
units.idiomatic: When Sima Yan became emperor, he made her empress.

units.zh: 有司奏依漢故事，皇后、太子各食湯沐邑四十縣，而帝以非古典，不許。
units.literal: The offices memorialized that, following Han precedent, the empress and crown prince should each receive forty counties as bath-and-maintenance fiefs, but the emperor held this was not ancient practice and did not permit it.
units.idiomatic: Officials asked that, as under Han custom, empress and heir each receive forty counties as bath-town fiefs, but the emperor refused as non-canonical.

units.zh: 后追懷舅氏之恩，顯官趙俊，納俊兄虞女粲於後宮為夫人。
units.literal: The empress recalled her debt to her mother’s clan, promoted Zhao Jun to high office, and brought Jun’s elder brother’s daughter Can into the inner palace as Honored Lady.
units.idiomatic: Remembering her uncle’s kindness, she advanced Zhao Jun and took his brother’s daughter Zhao Can into the palace as Honored Lady.

units.zh: 帝以皇太子不堪奉大統，密以語后。
units.literal: The emperor considered the crown prince unable to uphold the great line and secretly spoke of it to the empress.
units.idiomatic: Believing the crown prince unfit to inherit the realm, he confided as much privately to the empress.

units.zh: 后曰：「立嫡以長不以賢，豈可動乎？」
units.literal: The empress said: “Establishing the heir depends on seniority among legitimate sons, not on talent—how can that be altered?”
units.idiomatic: She replied, “The eldest legitimate son succeeds regardless of talent—how can we undo that?”

units.zh: 初，賈充妻郭氏使賂后，求以女為太子妃。
units.literal: At first Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo sent bribes to the empress, seeking to make her daughter crown princess.
units.idiomatic: Earlier Jia Chong’s wife Lady Guo had bribed her to secure her daughter as crown princess.

units.zh: 及議太子婚，帝欲娶衛瓘女。
units.literal: When discussing the crown prince’s marriage, the emperor wished to take Wei Guan’s daughter.
units.idiomatic: When the heir’s marriage came under debate, the emperor favored Wei Guan’s daughter.

units.zh: 然后盛稱賈后有淑德，又密使太子太傅荀顗進言，上乃聽之。
units.literal: But the empress greatly praised Consort Jia’s virtuous conduct, and also secretly had Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince Xun Yi speak; the sovereign then consented.
units.idiomatic: The empress loudly praised Lady Jia’s virtue and secretly had Grand Tutor Xun Yi speak for her, so the emperor yielded.

units.zh: 泰始中，帝博選良家以充後宮，先下書禁天下嫁娶，使宦者乘使車，給騶騎，馳傳州郡，召充選者使后揀擇。
units.literal: In the Taishi era the emperor broadly selected good families to fill the rear palace; first he issued a document forbidding marriage in the realm, had eunuchs ride dispatch coaches provided with outriders, gallop relay orders to provinces and commanderies, summon those filling selection and had the empress pick and choose.
units.idiomatic: Midway through Taishi he cast a wide net for palace women, banned commoners from marrying, sent eunuchs in official carriages with escorts racing along post roads to every commandery, and had the candidates presented to the empress for her verdict.

units.zh: 后性妒，惟取潔白長大，其端正美麗者並不見留。
units.literal: The empress was by nature jealous; she only took those fair and tall; those properly beautiful were none of them retained.
units.idiomatic: Jealous by nature, she kept only fair-skinned, tall girls and rejected every truly lovely face.

units.zh: 時卞藩女有美色，帝掩扇謂后曰：「卞氏女佳。」
units.literal: At the time Bian Fan’s daughter had beautiful looks; the emperor hid behind a fan and said to the empress: “Bian’s daughter is excellent.”
units.idiomatic: When Bian Fan’s daughter proved breathtaking, the emperor hid behind his fan and said, “The Bian girl is a jewel.”

units.zh: 后曰：「藩三世后族，其女不可枉以卑位。」
units.literal: The empress said: “The Bian clan for three generations has been empress kin—their daughter cannot be slighted with low rank.”
units.idiomatic: The empress answered, “Three generations of Bians have supplied empresses—such a bride cannot be parked in a petty title.”

units.zh: 帝乃止。
units.literal: The emperor then stopped.
units.idiomatic: He dropped the matter.

units.zh: 司徒李胤、鎮軍大將軍胡奮、廷尉諸葛沖、太僕臧權、侍中馮蓀、秘書郎左思及世族子女並充三夫人九嬪之列。
units.literal: Minister of Education Li Yin, General Who Guards the Army Hu Fen, Commandant of Justice Zhuge Chong, Grand Coachman Zang Quan, Palace Attendant Feng Sun, Secretary Court Gentleman Zuo Si, and daughters of eminent clans together filled the ranks of three ladies and nine bin.
units.idiomatic: The daughters of Li Yin, Hu Fen, Zhuge Chong, Zang Quan, Feng Sun, Zuo Si, and other great houses were placed among the Three Ladies and the Nine Concubines.

units.zh: 名家盛族子女，多敗衣瘁貌以避之。
units.literal: Sons and daughters of famous houses and great clans mostly wore tattered clothes and haggard looks to avoid it.
units.idiomatic: Great families dressed their girls in rags and smeared their faces to dodge the draft.

units.zh: 及后有疾，見帝素幸胡夫人，恐後立之，慮太子不安。
units.literal: When the empress had illness, she saw the emperor always favored Lady Hu and feared she would later be established, worrying for the crown prince’s security.
units.idiomatic: When she fell ill and saw how he favored Lady Hu, she feared a future empress would threaten her son.

units.zh: 臨終，枕帝膝曰：「叔父駿女男胤有德色，願陛下以備六宮。」
units.literal: At the end, pillowing on the emperor’s knee she said: “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin has virtue and beauty; I beg Your Majesty to keep her for the six palaces.”
units.idiomatic: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”

units.zh: 因悲泣，帝流涕許之。
units.literal: Thereupon she wept sadly; the emperor promised with flowing tears.
units.idiomatic: She wept; he swore through tears to comply.

units.zh: 泰始十年，崩於明光殿，絕于帝膝，時年三十七。
units.literal: In the tenth Taishi year she died in Mingguang Hall, expired on the emperor’s knee, aged thirty-seven.
units.idiomatic: She died in 274 in Mingguang Hall on his lap, thirty-seven years old.

units.zh: 詔曰：「皇后逮事先后，常冀能終始永奉宗廟，一旦殂隕，痛悼傷懷。
units.literal: An edict said: “The empress served the late consorts in succession, always hoping to be able from beginning to end forever to serve the ancestral temple; suddenly she has fallen—pain and grief wound the heart.
units.idiomatic: The edict read, “The empress served my late mothers and hoped to honor the shrines to the end; her sudden death tears my heart.

units.zh: 從之。
units.literal: It was approved.
units.idiomatic: Approved.

units.zh: 會昌元年六月，制曰：「朕近因載誕之日，展承顏之敬，太皇太后謂朕曰：『天子之孝，莫大於丕承；人倫之義，莫大于嗣續。穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝厭代已久，星霜屢遷，禰宮曠合食之禮，惟帝深濡露之感。宣懿皇太后，長慶之際，德冠後宮，夙表沙麓之祥，實茂河洲之範。先朝恩禮之厚，中壺莫偕。況誕我聖君，纘承昌運，已協華於先帝，方延祚於後昆。思廣貽謀，庶弘博愛，爰從舊典，以慰孝思。當以宣懿皇太后祔太廟穆宗睿聖文惠孝皇帝之室。率是彝訓，其敬承之。』朕祇奉慈旨，載深感咽。宜令宣示中外，咸使聞知。」會昌六年五月，禮儀使奏：武宗昭肅皇帝祔廟，併合祧遷者。伏以自敬宗、文宗、武宗兄弟相及，已歷三朝。昭穆之位，與承前不同。所可疑者，其事有四：一者，兄弟昭穆同位，不相為後；二者，已祧之主，復入舊廟；三者，廟數有限，無後之主，則宜出置別廟；四者，兄弟既不相為後，昭為父道，穆為子道，則昭穆同班，不合異位。據《春秋》「文公二年，躋僖公」。何休云：「躋，升也，謂西上也。惠公與莊公當同南面西上，隱、桓與閔、僖當同北面西上。」孔穎達亦引此義釋經。又賀循云：「殷之盤庚，不序陽甲；漢之光武，上繼元帝。」晉元帝、簡文，皆用此義毀之，蓋以昭穆位同，不可兼毀二廟故也。《尚書》曰：「七代之廟，可以觀德。」且殷家兄弟相及，有至四帝不及祖禰，何容更言七代，於理無矣。二者，今已兄弟相及，同為一代，矯前之失，則合復祔代宗神主於太廟。或疑已祧之主，不合更入太廟者。按晉代元、明之時，已遷豫章、潁川矣，及簡文即位，乃元帝之子，故復豫章、潁川二神主於廟。又國朝中宗已祔太廟，至開元四年，乃出置別廟，至十年，置九廟，而中宗神主復祔太廟。則已遷復入，亦可無疑。三者，廟有定數，無後之主，出置別廟者。按魏、晉之初多同廟，蓋取上古清廟一宮，尊遠神祗之義。自後晉武所立之廟，雖云七主，而實六代，蓋景、文同廟故也。又按魯立姜嫄、文王之廟，不計昭穆，以尊尚功德也。晉元帝上繼武帝，而惠、懷、湣三帝，時賀循等諸儒議，以為別立廟，親遠義疏，都邑遷異，於理無嫌也。今以文宗棄代才六七年，武宗甫邇復土，遽移別廟，不齒祖宗，在於有司，非所宜議。四者，添置廟之室。按《禮論》，晉太常賀循云：「廟以容主為限，無拘常數。」故晉武帝時，廟有七主六代。至元帝、明帝，廟皆十室。及成、康、穆三帝，皆至十一室。自後雖遷故祔新，大抵以七代為准，而不限室數。伏以江左大儒，通賾睹奧，事有明據，固可施行。今若不行是議，更以迭毀為制，則當上不及高曾未盡之親，下有忍臣子恩義之道。今備討古今，參校經史，上請復代宗神主於太廟，以存高曾之親。下以敬宗、文宗、武宗同為一代，於太廟東間添置兩室，定為九代十一室之制，以全臣子恩敬之義，庶協大順之宜，得變禮之正，折古今之紛互，立群疑之杓指。俾因心廣孝，永燭於皇明；昭德事神，無虧於聖代。敕曰：「宗廟事重，實資參詳。宜令尚書省、兩省、御史臺四品以上官、大理卿、京兆尹等集議以聞。」尚書左丞鄭涯等奏議曰：「夫禮經垂則，莫重于嚴配，必參損益之道，則合典禮之文。
units.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Huichang, an edict said: "Recently, on the day of my birth anniversary, when I displayed the reverence of attending upon her countenance, the Grand Empress Dowager told me: 'Of the filial duty of the Son of Heaven, nothing is greater than grandly continuing the succession; of the obligations of human relations, nothing is greater than heirs continuing the line. Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Benevolent, and Filial, has long since left the age, and years and seasons have repeatedly passed. His paternal temple chamber lacks the rite of sharing food, and only the emperor deeply feels the grief of dew and frost. Empress Dowager Xuanyi, in the Changqing era, surpassed the rear palace in virtue, early displayed the auspicious sign of Shalu, and truly flourished in the model of Hezhou. In the former reign the thickness of grace and ritual had no equal within the inner palace. How much more, since she gave birth to our sage ruler and continued the prosperous fortune, already sharing splendor with the former emperor and about to extend blessing to later descendants. Thinking to broaden the plans left to posterity and hoping to enlarge universal love, follow the old canon and so comfort filial thoughts. Empress Dowager Xuanyi should be attached in the Great Temple to the chamber of Emperor Muzong, the Sagely, Cultured, Benevolent, and Filial. Take this constant instruction as your model, and reverently carry it out.' I have respectfully received the compassionate command and am deeply moved and choked with feeling. Let it be proclaimed inside and outside, so that all may hear and know it." In the fifth month of the sixth year of Huichang, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol memorialized that when Emperor Wuzong, the Illustrious and Solemn, was attached to the temple, the tablets to be removed should also be considered together. Respectfully, since Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong succeeded one another as brothers, three reigns have already passed. Their zhao and mu positions differ from the former pattern. There are four matters that may be doubted. First, brothers occupy the same zhao-mu position and do not become successors to one another. Second, a tablet already removed may again enter the old temple. Third, the number of temple chambers is limited, and a tablet without a successor should be taken out and placed in a separate temple. Fourth, since brothers do not become successors to one another, zhao is the way of the father and mu is the way of the son; if zhao and mu are in the same rank, they should not occupy different positions. According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, "In the second year of Duke Wen, Duke Xi was raised." He Xiu says, "Raised means promoted, meaning westward precedence. Duke Hui and Duke Zhuang should face south together, with the westward place highest; Duke Yin, Duke Huan, Duke Min, and Duke Xi should face north together, with the westward place highest." Kong Yingda also cited this meaning in explaining the classic. He Xun also said, "Pangeng of Yin did not arrange Yangjia in sequence; Guangwu of Han continued upward from Emperor Yuan." Emperor Yuan and Emperor Jianwen of Jin both used this principle in removing temples, probably because when zhao and mu positions are the same, two temples cannot both be removed. The Book of Documents says, "In the temples of seven generations, virtue may be observed." Moreover, in the Yin house brothers succeeded one another, at times with four emperors not reaching grandfather or father; how could one then further speak of seven generations? In principle this is impossible. Second, now that brothers have succeeded one another and together form one generation, correcting the former error means that Emperor Daizong's spirit tablet should again be attached in the Great Temple. Some may doubt that a tablet already removed should again enter the Great Temple. But in the Jin, during the times of Yuan and Ming, Yuzhang and Yingchuan had already been moved out; when Jianwen ascended the throne, he was Emperor Yuan's son, and so the two spirit tablets of Yuzhang and Yingchuan were restored to the temple. Also, in our dynasty Zhongzong had already been attached in the Great Temple; in the fourth year of Kaiyuan he was taken out and placed in a separate temple, but in the tenth year, when nine temples were established, Zhongzong's spirit tablet was again attached in the Great Temple. Thus there should also be no doubt about restoring a tablet that has already been moved. Third, as for the temple having a fixed number and placing a tablet without a successor in a separate temple: at the beginning of Wei and Jin many shared the same temple, probably taking the ancient meaning of one clear temple hall and honoring remote deities. Afterward, in the temple established by Emperor Wu of Jin, though it was called seven tablets, it was in fact six generations, because Jing and Wen shared one temple. Again, Lu established temples for Jiang Yuan and King Wen without counting zhao and mu, in order to honor merit and virtue. Emperor Yuan of Jin continued upward from Emperor Wu, while for the three emperors Hui, Huai, and Min, the scholars He Xun and others debated at the time and considered that separate temples should be established; with kinship distant and obligation sparse, and with capital city and territory changed, there was no impropriety in principle. Now Wenzong has left the age only six or seven years ago, and Wuzong has only just recently returned to the earth; suddenly moving them to separate temples and not ranking them among the ancestors is not something the responsible offices should discuss. Fourth, as to adding temple chambers: according to the Discussion of Rites, He Xun, Chamberlain for Ceremonials of Jin, said, "A temple is limited by its capacity to hold tablets and is not bound to a constant number." Therefore, in Emperor Wu of Jin's time, the temple had seven tablets and six generations. By the time of Emperors Yuan and Ming, the temples both had ten chambers. With Emperors Cheng, Kang, and Mu, they all reached eleven chambers. Afterward, although old tablets were moved and new ones attached, in general seven generations served as the standard, but the number of chambers was not limited. Respectfully, the great scholars south of the Yangzi understood subtlety and saw what was profound; since the matter has clear evidence, it may certainly be carried out. If this proposal is not now carried out, and alternating removal is instead made the rule, then above it will fail to reach the not-yet-exhausted kinship of great-grandfather and grandfather, and below there will be the way of a minister and son enduring the loss of grace and obligation. Having now fully examined ancient and recent cases and compared classics and histories, we request above that Emperor Daizong's spirit tablet be restored to the Great Temple, preserving the kinship of great-grandfather and grandfather. Below, with Jingzong, Wenzong, and Wuzong together forming one generation, add two chambers in the eastern bay of the Great Temple and fix the system as nine generations and eleven chambers, in order to complete the obligation of grace and reverence owed by ministers and sons. This will nearly accord with the propriety of great obedience, obtain the correctness of adapting ritual, settle the disputes of ancient and recent times, and establish a handle and guide for all doubts. It will let filial piety broaden from the heart and forever shine in imperial brightness; it will manifest virtue in serving the spirits and leave no deficiency in the sage age. An edict said: "The matter of the ancestral temple is weighty and truly requires joint deliberation. Let the Department of State Affairs, the two Secretariats, officials of the fourth rank and above in the Censorate, the Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, the Intendant of Jingzhao, and others assemble and debate it for report." Vice Minister of the Left in the Department of State Affairs Zheng Ya and others memorialized in deliberation, saying: "The ritual classics hand down standards, and nothing is weightier than solemnly pairing the ancestors. One must consult the principle of adding and reducing; then it accords with the texts of canonical ritual.

units.idiomatic: Clear precedents supported a balanced ruling.

units.zh: 有星孛于胃。
units.literal: A broom star appeared in the asterism Wei.
units.idiomatic: A comet trailed through the Wei mansion.

units.zh: 乙未，帝將射雉，慮損麥苗而止。
units.literal: On the day yiwei the emperor was about to shoot pheasants but stopped, fearing damage to the wheat.
units.idiomatic: Yiwei: he canceled a hunt lest arrows trample the wheat.

units.zh: 夏五月戊子，吳將邵凱、夏祥帥眾七千餘人來降。
units.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day wuzi, Wu generals Shao Kai and Xia Xiang led more than seven thousand men to surrender.
units.idiomatic: Summer, wuzi: Shao Kai and Xia Xiang brought seven thousand Wu soldiers over.

title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

units.zh: 父充，別有傳。
units.literal: Her father Chong has separate biography.
units.idiomatic: Her father Jia Chong has his own biography.

units.zh: 初，武帝欲為太子取衛瓘女，元后納賈郭親黨之說，欲婚賈氏。
units.literal: At first Emperor Wu wished crown prince to marry Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yuan listened to Jia and Guo faction urging marriage with Jia clan.
units.idiomatic: Wu favored Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yang Yan pushed Jia kin.

units.zh: 帝曰：「衛公女有五可，賈公女有五不可。
units.literal: Emperor said: “Lord Wei’s daughter has five goods—Lord Jia’s daughter five bads.
units.idiomatic: Wu said, “Wei’s girl scores five merits—Jia’s five flaws.

units.zh: 衛家種賢而多子，美而長白；
units.literal: Wei house breeds wise and many sons—beautiful, tall, fair;
units.idiomatic: Weis are fertile and wise—fair and statuesque;

units.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。
units.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.
units.idiomatic: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.

units.zh: 帝常疑太子不慧，且朝臣和嶠等多以為言，故欲試之。
units.literal: Emperor often suspected crown prince dull—and ministers such as He Qiao said same—so wished to test him.
units.idiomatic: Wu doubted the heir’s wit—He Qiao agreed—so he tested him.

units.zh: 盡召東宮大小官屬，為設宴會，而密封疑事，使太子決之，停信待反。
units.literal: He summoned all eastern palace officials large and small, set banquet, sealed doubtful affairs ordering crown prince to decide—stopped courier awaiting reply.
units.idiomatic: He feasted Eastern Palace staff, sealed riddling cases for the heir to solve.

units.zh: 泓素有小才，具草，令太子自寫。
units.literal: Hong always had small talent—drafted fully—ordered crown prince himself copy.
units.idiomatic: Hong drafted; she made the prince copy.

units.zh: 帝省之，甚悅。
units.literal: Emperor examined—greatly pleased.
units.idiomatic: Wu read it—delighted.

units.zh: 先示太子少傅衛瓘，瓘大踧踖，眾人乃知瓘先有毀言，殿上皆稱萬歲。
units.literal: First showed Junior Mentor Wei Guan—Guan greatly ashamed—all knew Guan earlier had slanderous words—hall cheered ten thousand years.
units.idiomatic: He flashed it at Wei Guan—Wei squirmed; courtiers jeered Guan’s prior slanders.

units.zh: 或以戟擲孕妾，子隨刃墮地。
units.literal: Sometimes threw halberd at pregnant concubine—child fell with blade to ground.
units.idiomatic: She hurled a ji at a pregnant girl—the infant fell with the blow.

units.zh: 帝聞之，大怒，已修金墉城，將廢之。
units.literal: Emperor hearing greatly furious—already repaired Metal-Walled Fortress—about to depose her.
units.idiomatic: Wu rebuilt Jinyong cage ready to depose her.

units.zh: 充華趙粲從容言曰：「賈妃年少，妒是婦人之情耳，長自當差。
units.literal: Honorable Lady Zhao Can calmly said: “Consort Jia still young—jealousy is woman’s feeling—long maturity will correct.
units.idiomatic: Zhao Can soothed him: “She’s young—jealousy passes.

units.zh: 願陛下察之。」
units.literal: May Your Majesty investigate.”
units.idiomatic: May Your Majesty weigh this carefully."

units.zh: 其後楊珧亦為之言曰：「陛下忘賈公閭耶？」
units.literal: Later Yang Zhao also spoke for her: “Your Majesty forgot Lord Jia Chong?”
units.idiomatic: Yang Zhao added, “Remember Jia Chong?”

units.zh: 荀勖深救之，故得不廢。
units.literal: Xun Xu deeply rescued her—thus avoided deposition.
units.idiomatic: Xun Xu pleaded—she kept rank.

units.zh: 初，誅楊駿及汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋等，皆臨機專斷，宦人董猛參預其事。
units.literal: At first executing Yang Jun and Prince Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—all improvised executions—eunuch Dong Meng participated.
units.idiomatic: Yang Jun, Sima Liang, Wei Guan, Sima Wei died by her whim—with eunuch Dong Meng.

units.zh: 猛，武帝時為寺人監，侍東宮，得親信于后，預誅楊駿，封武安侯，猛三兄皆為亭侯，天下咸怨。
units.literal: Meng—Wu-era Inner Palace Overseer—served Eastern Palace—won consort trust—participated executing Yang Jun—enfeoffed Marquis Wu’an—Meng three elder brothers all village marquis—all realm resented.
units.idiomatic: Dong Meng gained titles—his brothers too—the realm cursed them.

units.zh: 及太子廢黜，趙王倫、孫秀等因眾怨謀欲廢后[8]。
units.literal: When crown prince deposed—Prince Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu exploiting resentment plotted depose consort [8].
units.idiomatic: Once Minhuai fell Sima Lun and Sun Xiu used hatred to target her [8].

title.zh: 卷16 志第11 律曆上
title.en: Volume 16 Treatises 11: Measures and the Calendar 1
title.raw: 卷16 志第11 律曆上 Volume 16 Treatises 11: Measures and the Calendar 1

units.zh: 祖沖之所傳銅尺。
units.literal: The copper foot measure transmitted by Zu Chongzhi.
units.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi's transmitted copper foot measure.

units.zh: 徐廣、徐爰、王隱等《晉書》云：「武帝泰始九年，中書監荀勖校太樂八音，不和，始知為後漢至魏，尺長於古四分有餘。
units.literal: Xu Guang, Xu Ai, Wang Yin, and others' Jin History says: "In Emperor Wu's Taishi ninth year, Director of the Secretariat Xun Xu corrected the Grand Music eight timbres—they were not harmonious; then knowing that from Later Han through Wei the foot measure was more than four fen longer than antiquity.
units.idiomatic: The Jin History of Xu Guang, Xu Yuan, Wang Yin, and others records: "In the ninth year of Taishi, Xun Xu, Supervisor of the Secretariat, checked the eight timbres of the Grand Music and found them discordant; only then did he understand that from Later Han to Wei the chi had grown more than four fen longer than the ancient measure.

units.zh: 勖乃部著作郎劉恭，依《周禮》制尺，所謂古尺也。
units.literal: Xu then ordered Editorial Director Liu Gong to make a foot measure according to the Rites of Zhou—the so-called ancient foot measure.
units.idiomatic: Xu ordered Liu Gong to make a Rites of Zhou foot measure—the ancient standard.

title.zh: 卷三十五 列傳第五 陳騫 裴秀
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 5: Chen Qian; Pei Xiu
title.raw: 卷三十五 列傳第五 陳騫 裴秀 Volume 35 Biographies 5: Chen Qian; Pei Xiu

units.zh: 又轉都督江南諸軍事，徙都督荊州諸軍事、征南大將軍，封郯侯。
units.literal: He was again made area commander south of the Yangzi, then transferred to area commander for Jingzhou and General Who Conquers the South, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Tan.
units.idiomatic: His command shifted to the southland, then to Jingzhou as General Who Conquers the South, with a marquisate at Tan.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，以佐命之勳，進車騎將軍，封高平郡公，遷侍中、大將軍，出為都督揚州諸軍事，餘如故，假黃鉞。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, Qian was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry for his merit among the founding ministers, enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoping commandery, advanced to Palace Attendant and Grand General, and sent out as area commander for Yangzhou's armies, his other posts unchanged; he was also granted the yellow battle-axe.
units.idiomatic: After Sima Yan founded the Jin, Qian's founding service earned him the chariots-and-cavalry command, the ducal fief of Gaoping, posts as palace attendant and grand general, command of Yangzhou, and the ceremonial axe that marked supreme delegated authority.

units.zh: 攻拔吳枳裏城，破塗中屯戍。
units.literal: He stormed and took the Wu stronghold at Zhili and destroyed the garrison at Tuzhong.
units.idiomatic: He seized Wu's Zhili fortress and dismantled the encampment at Tuzhong.

units.zh: 咸甯初，遷太尉，轉大司馬。
units.literal: In the early Xianning era he was promoted to Grand Commandant, then to Grand Marshal.
units.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianning reign he became Grand Commandant, then Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 騫因入朝，言於帝曰：「胡烈、牽弘皆勇而無謀，強于自用，非綏邊之材，將為國恥。
units.literal: Qian then entered court and said to the emperor, "Hu Lie and Qian Hong are both brave but without strategy and are forceful in following their own judgment. They are not men fit to pacify the frontier and will become a disgrace to the state.
units.idiomatic: Qian then entered court and said to the emperor, "Hu Lie and Qian Hong are both brave but without strategy and are forceful in following their own judgment. They are not men fit to pacify the frontier and will become a disgrace to the state.

units.zh: 願陛下詳之。」
units.literal: I hope Your Majesty will examine this carefully."
units.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will examine this carefully."

units.zh: 時弘為揚州刺史，不承順騫命。
units.literal: At the time Qian Hong was Governor of Yangzhou and refused to obey Qian's orders.
units.idiomatic: Hong was then governor of Yangzhou and would not follow Qian's directives.

units.zh: 帝以為不協相構，於是征弘，既至，尋復以為涼州刺史。
units.literal: The emperor assumed the two men were feuding and slandering each other, so he summoned Hong; after Hong arrived he soon appointed him Governor of Liangzhou again.
units.idiomatic: The ruler took their clash for mutual spite, recalled Hong, then almost immediately sent him west as governor of Liangzhou once more.

units.zh: 騫竊歎息，以為必敗。
units.literal: Qian sighed to himself, convinced disaster would follow.
units.idiomatic: Qian privately groaned, certain the policy would end badly.

units.zh: 二人後果失羌戎之和，皆被寇喪沒，征討連歲，僅而得定，帝乃悔之。
units.literal: The two men afterward alienated the Qiang and Rong peoples; both died under barbarian attack, and campaigns dragged on for years before order was barely restored. The emperor then regretted his decision.
units.idiomatic: Both later shattered tribal alliances, fell to raids, and cost years of campaigning before the frontier steadied—only then did the court regret ignoring Qian.

units.zh: 騫少有度量，含垢匿瑕，所在有績。
units.literal: Qian had possessed forbearance since youth; he swallowed insults and overlooked faults, and wherever he served he left a record of achievement.
units.idiomatic: From boyhood Qian bore slights lightly and governed effectively wherever he was posted.

units.zh: 咸寧三年，求入朝，因乞骸骨。
units.literal: In the third year of Xianning, he asked leave to come to the capital and petitioned to retire on grounds of old age.
units.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianning, he sought permission to return to Luoyang and yield his office, pleading age and infirmity.

units.zh: 賜袞冕之服，詔曰：「騫元勳舊德，統乂東夏，方弘遠績，以一吳會，而所苦未除，每表懇切，重勞以方事。
units.literal: He was granted the robe with gun-dragon and coronet, and the edict said, "Qian has old virtue and founding merit, governs and orders the eastern Xia, and is about to broaden distant achievements by unifying Wu and Kuaiji. But his affliction has not been removed, and whenever he memorializes earnestly, we again burden him with current affairs.
units.idiomatic: He was granted the robe with gun-dragon and coronet, and the edict said, "Qian has old virtue and founding merit, governs and orders the eastern Xia, and is about to broaden distant achievements by unifying Wu and Kuaiji. But his affliction has not been removed, and whenever he memorializes earnestly, we again burden him with current affairs.

units.zh: 今聽留京城，以前太尉府為大司馬府，增置祭酒二人，帳下司馬、官騎、大車、鼓吹皆如前，親兵百人，廚田十頃，廚園五十畝，廚士十人，器物經用皆留給焉。
units.literal: Now he is permitted to remain in the capital. The former Grand Commandant's office is to be made the Grand Marshal's office; two Libationers are to be added, and his tent staff, office cavalry, great carriages, and drums and pipes are all to be as before. A hundred personal troops, ten qing of kitchen fields, fifty mu of kitchen gardens, ten kitchen workers, and vessels and regular expenses are all to remain supplied to him.
units.idiomatic: Now he is permitted to remain in the capital. The former Grand Commandant's office is to be made the Grand Marshal's office; two Libationers are to be added, and his tent staff, office cavalry, great carriages, and drums and pipes are all to be as before. A hundred personal troops, ten qing of kitchen fields, fifty mu of kitchen gardens, ten kitchen workers, and vessels and regular expenses are all to remain supplied to him.

units.zh: 遂固請，許之，位同保傅，在三司之上，賜以几杖，不朝，安車駟馬，以高平公還第。
units.literal: He pressed his request until it was granted. His rank equaled that of the elder tutors, standing above the Three Dukes; he received a seat and staff, was excused from court, given a comfortable carriage and four-horse team, and sent to his estate as Duke of Gaoping.
units.idiomatic: At last his resignation stood: he was ranked above the three highest ministers like an imperial mentor, with chair, staff, freedom from court audience, a coach and four, and the title of Duke of Gaoping while living privately.

units.zh: 帝以其勳舊耆老，禮之甚重。
units.literal: The emperor, honoring him as a founding elder, treated him with exceptional ceremony.
units.idiomatic: As a dynastic founder now grown old, Qian received extraordinary deference from the throne.

units.zh: 又以騫有疾，聽乘輿上殿。
units.literal: Because Qian was unwell, he was permitted to be carried in a litter into the hall.
units.idiomatic: Ill health won him the privilege of a litter right up to the audience hall.

units.zh: 騫素無謇諤之風，然與帝語傲；
units.literal: Qian had never been outspoken, yet in speaking with the emperor he carried himself with pride;
units.idiomatic: He was not known for blunt remonstrance, but he spoke to the sovereign with something like insolence,

units.zh: 及見皇太子加敬，時人以為諂。
units.literal: when he met the crown prince he showed deference, and people of the day took it for flattery.
units.idiomatic: yet before the heir apparent he became deferential, which contemporaries dismissed as sycophancy.

units.zh: 元康二年薨，年八十一，加以袞斂，贈太傅，諡曰武。
units.literal: In the second year of Yuankang, he died at eighty-one. He was buried in ducal vestments, posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, with the posthumous name Martial.
units.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuankang, he died at eighty-one, laid out in princely robes, ennobled posthumously as Grand Tutor with the epithet "Martial."

units.zh: 及葬，帝于大司馬門臨喪，望柩流涕，禮依大司馬石苞故事。
units.literal: At the burial the emperor came to the Grand Marshal Gate to mourn, gazed at the coffin and wept; the rites followed the precedent for Grand Marshal Shi Bao.
units.idiomatic: The sovereign mourned him at the Grand Marshal Gate, weeping over the bier as had been done for Grand Marshal Shi Bao.

units.zh: 子輿嗣爵。=
units.literal: His son Yu inherited the noble title.
units.idiomatic: The noble title passed to his son Yu.

title.raw: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wu

units.zh: 太廟成。
units.literal: The grand ancestral temple was completed.
units.idiomatic: The new imperial temple stood finished.

units.zh: 乙巳，遷神主于新廟，帝迎于道左，遂祫祭。
units.literal: On the day yisi the spirit tablets were moved to the new temple; the emperor welcomed them on the left of the road, then performed the joint sacrifice.
units.idiomatic: Yisi: ancestral tablets entered the new shrine in a procession the emperor met in person, followed by a combined offering.

units.zh: 大赦，文武增位一等，作廟者二等。
units.literal: A great amnesty was declared; civil and military officials were advanced one grade in rank, and those who built the temple two grades.
units.idiomatic: Amnesty came with promotions—one step for officials, two for temple builders.

units.zh: 十一月丙辰，守尚書令、左光祿大夫荀勖卒。
units.literal: On the day bingchen of the eleventh month Xun Xu, acting supervisor of the masters of writing and grand master for splendid happiness on the left, died.
units.idiomatic: Bingchen: Xun Xu died in office.

units.zh: 帝疾瘳，賜王公以下帛有差。
units.literal: When the emperor’s illness abated, silks were bestowed on the kings and dukes downward, each according to difference.
units.idiomatic: On partial recovery he handed out graded silk to the nobility.

units.zh: 含章殿鞠室火。
units.literal: The ball-court chamber in the Hanzhang hall caught fire.
units.idiomatic: Fire broke out in the Hanzhang hall’s indoor ball court.

title.raw: 卷二十五 志第十五 輿服 Volume 25 Treatises 15: Travel and Dress

units.zh: 羊車，一名輦車，其上如軺，伏兔箱，漆畫輪軛。
units.literal: The goat cart, one name is palanquin cart; its upper part is like a ya cart, with crouching-rabbit boxes, lacquered painted wheels and yoke.
units.idiomatic: The “goat cart,” also called litter-style wagon, has a light upperworks like a patrol car, hare-shaped boxes, and lacquered wheels.

units.zh: 武帝時，護軍羊琇輒乘羊車，司隸劉毅糾劾其罪。
units.literal: In Emperor Wu’s time, the household guard Yang Xiu always rode a goat cart, and the metropolitan inspector Liu Yi impeached his offense.
units.idiomatic: Under Jin Wudi, Guard-general Yang Xiu habitually rode a goat-drawn cart until Liu Yi, metropolitan inspector, charged him for it.

units.zh: 畫輪車，駕牛，以彩漆畫輪轂，故名曰畫輪車。
units.literal: The painted-wheel cart is drawn by oxen; because colored lacquer paints the hubs, it is therefore called the painted-wheel cart.
units.idiomatic: Ox-drawn “painted-wheel” pleasure wagons take their name from their polychrome hub decoration.

units.zh: 象車，漢鹵簿最在前。
units.literal: The elephant cart was foremost in Han’s ceremonial escort.
units.idiomatic: Han processions once led with an elephant car.

units.zh: 武帝太康中平吳後，南越獻馴象，詔作大車駕之，以載黃門鼓吹數十人，使越人騎之。
units.literal: In Emperor Wu’s Taikang mid-period, after Wu was pacified, Southern Yue presented tame elephants; an edict ordered a great cart made to harness them, to carry several dozen yellow-gate musicians, with Yue men riding them.
units.idiomatic: After Jin conquered Wu in the Taikang era, Nanyue sent trained elephants; the court built huge wagons, loaded them with palace musicians, and seated southern handlers aloft.

units.zh: 元正大會，駕象入庭。
units.literal: At the New Year’s great assembly, elephants were driven into the courtyard.
units.idiomatic: New Year audiences opened with elephants paraded into the palace yard.

units.zh: 昔周命南仲，城彼朔方，趙靈、秦始，長城是築；
units.literal: Formerly Zhou appointed Nanzhong and walled that northern region; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin built the Long Wall;
units.idiomatic: Long ago Zhou commissioned Nanzhong to fortify the northern frontier; King Ling of Zhao and the First Emperor of Qin raised the Long Wall;

units.zh: 漢之孝武，踵其前事。
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Han followed their earlier deeds.
units.idiomatic: and Emperor Wu of Han followed their example.

units.zh: 此四代之君，皆帝王之雄傑，所以同此役者，非智術之不長，兵眾之不足，乃防狄之要事，理宜然也。
units.literal: These rulers of four dynasties were all heroic emperors and kings; the reason they all undertook this task was not that their wisdom and arts were insufficient or their troops inadequate, but that defending against the Di was an essential matter and reason demanded it.
units.idiomatic: These four rulers were all formidable sovereigns. They undertook the same labor not from lack of strategy or troops, but because guarding against the northern barbarians was essential—and rightly so.

units.zh: 耿弇字伯昭，扶風茂陵人也。
units.literal: Geng Yan, styled Bozhao, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng.
units.idiomatic: Geng Yan, courtesy name Bozhao, was a native of Maoling in Fufeng commandery.

units.zh: 其先武帝時以吏二千石自巨鹿徙焉。
units.literal: His ancestors, in the time of Emperor Wu, as officials at the rank of two thousand shi, moved from Julu to there.
units.idiomatic: His forebears had held a two-thousand-dan post under Emperor Wu and relocated from Julu to Maoling.

units.zh: 父況，字俠遊，以明經為郎，與王莽從弟伋共學《老子》於安丘先生，後為朔調連率。
units.literal: His father Kuang, styled Xiayou, through understanding the classics became a gentleman-attendant, and with Wang Mang's cousin Ji together studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, afterward became chain commandant of Shuodiao.
units.idiomatic: His father Geng Kuang, courtesy name Xiayou, entered court as a gentleman-attendant on the strength of his classical learning; with Wang Mang's cousin Wang Ji he studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, and was later appointed chain commandant of the Shuodiao circuit.

units.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
units.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.
